\chapter{Synthesis --- Describing Where You Are}
\label{ch:synthesis-hay}
\hlchaptermodality{190}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can describe a place using existence, relative clauses and impersonal obligation together.}

Complete ES-C54-sintesis-lo-que-hay: build lo que hay, hay que comerlo and say what remains to be learned.

\section[Practice]{Synthesis — describing where you are}

\label{lesson:ES-C54-sintesis-lo-que-hay}



\begin{quote}
\emph{Hay} is the word you reach for to describe a place. Look around the room you are in and say what is there.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{The exchange}
\begin{quote}
— \emph{¿Qué hay aquí?} — \emph{\textbf{Hay} una casa. \textbf{Hay} libros — \textbf{los que} compré.} — \emph{¿Y \textbf{la comida que} haces?} — \emph{\textbf{Lo que} hay, \textbf{hay que} comerlo.}
\end{quote}

The last line is four words of grammar stacked on each other, and every piece came from a different chapter:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{lo que hay} — the noun-shaped hole, filled by \emph{hay}
  \item \emph{hay que} — obligation with nobody obliged
  \item \emph{comerlo} — the object pronoun, riding on the end of an infinitive
\end{itemize}

You have not been taught that last one, and you can still read it: \emph{comer} plus \emph{lo}. That is what it feels like when a language starts assembling itself.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={Grammar Lens: what you can do now}]
Describing a place is a small thing that needs a surprising amount: an existence word, articles that count, nouns, relative clauses to pick things out, and a way to say what has to happen. This chapter needed all of them, and you supplied them without any of it being new.

That is the honest end of a beginner's course. Not \textquotedblleft{}you are finished\textquotedblright{} — nobody is — but \textbf{the machinery is assembled}. Every remaining thing in Spanish is either a word you have not met yet or a familiar structure standing somewhere you have not seen it stand.

The eleven gaps found in the original audit are now closed. What is left is not a gap. It is the ordinary, unbounded work of using the thing.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item the whole four-line exchange
  \item \textquotedblleft{}Lo que hay, hay que comerlo\textquotedblright{} — and hear four chapters at once
\end{itemize}

\emph{Twice through:}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Ask what there is here. (\emph{\textbf{¿Qué hay aquí?}}) Say what there is, one must eat. (\emph{\textbf{Lo que hay, hay que comerlo}}.) And what is left after this? (\textbf{Words, and practice} — the machinery is assembled.)
\end{tcolorbox}
